title: Gain Acts Alone, Loss Needs Both

scenes.tts: A cell should divide only when it is told to. So every signaling pathway has an on-step and an off-step. The signal flips a switch on, and the off-step flips it back. Now suppose the switch sticks. The cell divides on its own. There are two ways to make that happen: jam an on-step, or remove an off-step.
scenes.visual: A growth signal flips a big switch on and the cell divides; the signal leaves, the off-step flips it back and the cell waits. Then the switch sticks on with no signal and the cell divides. Two chips name the two faults.

Now suppose the switch sticks. The cell divides on its own. There are two ways to make that happen: jam an on-step, or remove an off-step.

Now suppose the switch sticks. The cell divides on its own. There are two ways to make that happen: jam an on-step, or remove an off-step.

scenes.tts: First, jam the on-step. Ras is on while it holds G T P. Normally a helper called a G A P makes Ras break down that G T P, and the switch turns off. One changed amino acid, as in Ras G twelve V, slows this. Ras breaks down its G T P slowly, even with a G A P. A gene that can turn a cell cancerous is an oncogene.
scenes.visual: Normal Ras holds a GTP badge; a GAP arrives, the GTP is broken down and the cell waits. Reset to Ras G12V: the GAP arrives and is blocked, the GTP stays and the cell divides. An oncogene tag appears.
scenes.caption: First, jam the on-step. Ras is on while it holds GTP. Normally a helper called a GAP makes Ras break down that GTP, and the switch turns off. One changed amino acid, as in Ras G12V, slows this. Ras breaks down its GTP slowly, even with a GAP. A gene that can turn a cell cancerous is an oncogene.

One changed amino acid, as in Ras G12V, slows this. Ras breaks down its GTP slowly, even with a GAP. A gene that can turn a cell cancerous is an oncogene.

scenes.tts: Second, remove the off-step. Neurofibromin is a G A P for Ras. It is the off-step. Lose neurofibromin, and Ras G T P is not cleared. No on-step is jammed here. An off-step is missing. A gene whose loss lets cells grow when they should not is a tumour suppressor.
scenes.visual: Normal Ras holds GTP with neurofibromin, a GAP, beside it. The GAP is lost and a dashed empty slot remains; GTP is not cleared and the cell divides. Ras stays labelled normal. A tumour suppressor tag appears.
scenes.caption: Second, remove the off-step. Neurofibromin is a GAP for Ras. It is the off-step. Lose neurofibromin, and Ras-GTP is not cleared. No on-step is jammed here. An off-step is missing. A gene whose loss lets cells grow when they should not is a tumour suppressor.

scenes.tts: Now count the copies. You carry two copies of nearly every gene, one from each parent. Suppose one copy of the Ras gene is changed. The altered protein signals without being told to. The normal protein from the other copy cannot stop it. So the cell divides. This is a gain of function, and it is dominant. It shows even when the other copy is normal.
scenes.visual: Two copies of the Ras gene, one from each parent. One copy turns red and makes altered Ras that signals; the normal Ras from the other copy cannot stop it. The cell divides. Tags: gain of function, dominant.

scenes.tts: An off-switch is different. One good copy usually makes enough protein to do the job. Lose one copy of the gene, and the off-step still works. Both copies must go before the off-step fails. Alfred Knudson proposed two hits for retinoblastoma. The two hits turned out to be the two copies of one gene.
scenes.visual: Two copies of an off-switch gene, each making a GAP; the cell waits. One copy is lost, the other still makes GAP, and the cell waits. Then both are lost, no GAP is made, and the cell divides. Two hit marks land on the two copies.
scenes.caption: An off-switch is different. One good copy usually makes enough protein to do the job. Lose one copy of the gene, and the off-step still works. Both copies must go before the off-step fails. Alfred Knudson proposed two hits for retinoblastoma. The two hits turned out to be the two copies of one gene.

scenes.tts: So a stuck switch follows two rules, whichever way it sticks. A jammed on-step acts when one copy is altered. A lost off-step usually needs both copies gone. Gain acts alone. Loss needs both.
scenes.visual: Two rows of copy pairs. Jammed on-step: one altered copy of two, the cell divides. Lost off-step: one of two lost, the cell waits; both lost, the cell divides. Two closing words: gain acts alone, loss needs both.
